A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dejavu/EFN research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and content can be matched across the extensive restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO experiments, AgiBot-G1 manipulation results and component ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation and physical experiments, including additional CALVIN results, baseline comparisons, bank-management analyses and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The core retrieval-conditioned residual policy, SAC training and Sinkhorn reward remain. The reported critic representation changes from shared 512-dimensional projections in v1 Appendix B to four 1024-dimensional summaries in v2 B.3. v2 also omits v1 Appendix D's auxiliary compressed, language-aware reranking pipeline. Success-only deployment storage mainly reconciles conflicting v1 descriptions, since v1's evaluation already specified this rule.

E1.justification: v2 adds CALVIN's multi-goal manipulation and held-out-environment evaluation, plus the bimanual DrawerStore physical task. The earlier box-placement, shelf-grouping and restocking scenarios have renamed and re-specified counterparts; they are not three entirely new tasks.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's comparisons against unaugmented VLA backbones, v2 evaluates kNN-RAG, ResAct-style, R2A-style and GC-TTT-style comparators in Tables 1 and 2. GO-1 also newly participates in the LIBERO comparison. Appendix B describes the adapted baseline implementations.

E3.justification: New protocols include CALVIN ABC-to-D evaluation on 1,000 five-goal chains with Success@k and completed-chain length, runtime benchmarking, and direct-action controls. The retained reward ablation is also redescribed: v1 replaces Sinkhorn with cosine, whereas v2 removes dense rewards in favor of sparse returns. Identical scores and the retained figure legend do not establish that this experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of training-bank composition and reward distributions, success-only versus all-rollout deployment updates, residual versus direct action prediction, and computational costs across module configurations. Figures 11–14 and Tables 4 and 7–9 substantially extend v1's component and bank-capacity analyses.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies averaging over three evaluation seeds in Section 4.1 and Appendix B.4; v1 provides no comparable repeated-run protocol. This is additional reporting, not evidence that the number of runs increased. Confidence intervals and formal significance tests remain absent.

E6.justification: The common OpenVLA/UniVLA base and EFN Vol=300/1000 rows in Table 1 are numerically unchanged. v2 adds extensive comparator, GO-1, CALVIN, physical-task and diagnostic results. For example, its CALVIN OpenVLA Success@5 is 0.430 without EFN and 0.508 with Vol=5000; Table 9 reports 0% for direct-action EFN versus 87.0% for residual EFN. Revised physical-task results do not establish same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Substantial formal material disappears: v1 Appendix D's projected/quantized descriptors, relation and phase scoring, and fusion definitions, plus Appendix F's extended optimal-transport derivations, limiting properties and generalizations. v2 B.2 retains the core Sinkhorn score construction. The main SAC and anti-idling equations largely persist.

C1.justification: The central claim of improving frozen VLAs through experience memory remains. However, v2's introduction and conclusion substantially broaden the comparative contribution: EFN now claims superiority over retrieval-only, residual-only, retrieval-augmented RL and test-time-training alternatives under shared budgets, rather than merely improvements over frozen backbones.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of mixed-outcome training memories, success-only deployment updates, residual versus direct prediction, and transfer without nearly identical scenes. It adds limitations of automatic success detection and expands backbone-dependence discussion. Conversely, v1 Appendix E's detailed failed-training account and several retrieval, visual-alignment and residual-instability caveats are omitted.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation: JSON-based bank indexing, retrieval temperature, reward weights, replay capacity, training pseudocode, network internals, adapted baseline procedures, physical control and camera setup, and timing methodology. It also adds statements about supplementary code and demo availability and names video files. These disclosures do not by themselves establish changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against robotic retrieval and episodic-control approaches, adding works such as RAM, RT-Cache and STRAP. Its introduction explicitly distinguishes EFN's frozen policy and growing memory from trainable-policy or static-memory approaches, extending v1's more general retrieval and residual-learning background.

P1.justification: The title changes, the introduction and background are extensively rewritten, and the standalone preliminaries section disappears. Appendices are reorganized around implementation, design rationale, discussion, supplementary experiments and demonstrations, with earlier technical appendices condensed or removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, relocates the framework diagrams, expands comparison tables and adds numerous retrieval, reward, memory and efficiency displays. v1's residual visualization and ablation chart reappear as v2 Figures 7 and 8; these are redisplays rather than wholly new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: CALVIN evaluation, competing adaptation methods and detailed implementation information address important gaps in v1. However, v2 describes R2A and GC-TTT as updating the backbone while Appendix B.4 freezes it; Appendix B.5's 60–80-step physical horizon conflicts with Table 2's hundreds of steps. The reward ablation also changes meaning while retaining its scores and old figure label. These inconsistencies affect the principal new comparative evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
